question: On Thursday morning Aditi had 55 crates of oranges, more than her colleague Bram had picked. Each crate held 7 nets of fruit. Before noon a delivery added 66 nets, and Bram brought 67 nets in the early afternoon. In the evening the packhouse split every net into 9 punnets. Overnight the depot ordered 4 punnets for every punnet in the store. How many punnets does the depot's order come to?

On Monday morning a call centre had 88 headsets, which were shared equally between the 4 teams; the support team's share is the one being followed. In the afternoon the manager ordered 2 headsets for every headset that team had. In the evening head office went further, supplying 7 headsets for each one of those. A closing office then donated 64 headsets to the same team. The centre reports call lengths in minutes although its targets are set in hours. How many headsets does the support team have?

On Tuesday morning a printer received 126 reels of paper, and each reel was cut into 4 rolls. Before noon every roll was slit into 7 ribbons. In the afternoon the ribbons were shared equally between the 6 presses, and the evening press is the one being followed. That press then printed 6 tickets from every ribbon in its share. Late that night a partner shop sent over 74 finished tickets. The works covers 700 square metres, and the presses are timed in minutes although the schedule is written in hours. How many tickets does the evening press have?

A tool hire shop had 33 ladders on its rack. A firm that was closing sold it 58 ladders, and an auction added 79 more. A building contract then took 147 ladders away for the season. The shop ordered 7 ladders for every ladder left on the rack. Half of the yard is under cover, and hire is charged in hours although the paperwork is filled in by the minute. How many ladders does the order come to?

A juice bar bought 122 crates of carrots, and each crate held 6 bunches. Wilting spoiled 138 bunches, and a market trader sent over 67 fresh ones. The kitchen used 635 bunches during the month, and a soup stall took 14 more. Half of the cold room is given over to bottles. How many bunches does the juice bar have left?

A school orchestra had 239 sheets of music in its folder. The librarian withdrew 81 sheets that were falling apart. A composer sent 3 new sheets, and 55 sheets went to a partner school. The conductor then had 3 copies made of every sheet in the folder. The orchestra rehearses in hours although the registers are marked in minutes. How many sheets of music are there now?

A groundsman brought 72 rolls of turf onto the pitch, and each roll was cut into 8 strips. Laying the goalmouths used up 295 strips. A supplier delivered 79 strips, a neighbouring club gave 48, and the council sent 7 more. How many strips does the groundsman have now?

On Friday morning a school kitchen had 60 packs of pasta, and each pack made 4 portions. At midday the portions were shared equally between the 3 sittings, and the first sitting is the one being followed. In the afternoon the cook prepared 2 portions for every portion in that sitting. In the evening 53 portions from it were served to the after-school club. How many portions are left for the first sitting?

Fabio harvests more olives than his cousin Nella does. He filled 78 sacks, and each sack was tipped into 8 crates. Every crate was pressed into 4 bottles of oil, and each bottle was decanted into 3 small flasks. Nella added 70 flasks from her own press, and a co-op sent 21 more. Half of Fabio's cellar is below ground. How many flasks does Fabio have?

On Monday morning a brick kiln fired 107 trays, and each tray held 6 bricks. Before noon a lorry delivered 73 loose bricks. In the afternoon the works produced 4 bricks for every brick in the yard. During the evening 869 bricks went to a housing site, and overnight a builder collected 859 more. The yard is 45 metres across. How many bricks are left in the yard?

Amina prints more wallpaper than her partner Gustav does. She started with 163 rolls, and each roll was cut into 7 lengths. A shop bought 512 lengths. The mill then printed 9 lengths for every length she had left. A hotel contract took 2415 lengths, and a chain store finally ordered 8 lengths for every length remaining. The mill has 24 printing tables. How many lengths does the chain store's order come to?

On Saturday morning a market trader had 202 toy cars on his stall, and 11 of them were sold early on. A collector returned 6 cars that were the wrong model. At midday a wholesaler matched the stall exactly, leaving 2 cars for every car on it. In the afternoon a house clearance added 76 cars, and 125 cars were sold before closing. In the evening the wholesaler supplied 9 cars for every car left on the stall. How many cars does the trader have now?

On Thursday morning a pet shop had 77 water bowls, and a delivery added 35 more before noon. At midday a second delivery doubled the number of bowls in the shop. During the afternoon 87 bowls were sold. In the evening head office supplied 8 bowls for every bowl left on the shelf. A customer then returned 32 bowls that were the wrong size. How many bowls does the shop have?

On Monday morning a cannery received 234 sacks of tomatoes, and each sack filled 4 pots. By the afternoon every pot had been divided into 4 tins. In the evening 220 tins failed the seal test and were scrapped. Overnight the plant ran that same order for each of 3 supermarkets, needing that many tins per supermarket. The cannery lists cooking times in minutes although the labels give them in hours. How many tins does the whole order come to?

Hanna makes more picture frames than her colleague Ivo does. She had 237 frames in her workshop, and a gallery bought 164 of them. Ivo then delivered 55 frames he had built. A department store ordered 5 frames for every frame in the workshop. The frames were shared equally between the store's 5 branches, and the seafront branch's share is the one to follow. The workshop has been open 11 years. How many frames went to the seafront branch?

On Sunday morning Freya had 61 raffle prizes on the table, more than her co-organiser Sam had gathered. Before noon 28 prizes were claimed. At midday a shop donated 56 prizes, and Sam brought 51 more in the early afternoon. Later a bakery added 47 prizes. During the evening draw 127 prizes were handed out. How many prizes are left on the table?

A stationery warehouse had 112 boxes of pencils, and a returned order added 22 boxes. Each box was opened into 4 packs, and every pack held 8 pencils. A school then donated 78 loose pencils to the same store. The warehouse stands 300 metres from the station. How many pencils are in the store?

On Monday morning Rosa had 236 rolls of wire in her workshop, more than her colleague Timo had. She bought 13 rolls before lunch, and Timo gave her 54 in the early afternoon. In the evening the supplier cut every roll she owned into 9 lengths. A late delivery added 51 lengths, and half of her workshop is taken up by the bender. How many lengths does Rosa have?

Meera weaves more baskets than her cousin Anil does. She cut 101 bundles of willow, and each bundle produced 7 rods. Every rod was then split into 8 strands. Anil gave her 80 strands, and a supplier sent 11 more. The workshop is 25 years old. How many strands does Meera have?

A hospital laundry had 71 rolls of paper towel, and a supplier delivered 63 more. Each roll was cut into 9 packs. A ward then took 496 packs. The trust ordered 4 packs for every pack still in the store. Half of the store is refrigerated, and the trust bills its supplies in dollars although the invoices are itemised in cents. How many packs does the order come to?

A match factory filled 29 cases, and each case held 8 cartons. Every carton contained 6 boxes of matches. A shop bought 455 boxes. The factory then produced 2 boxes for every box it had left, and a second run made 7 boxes for each of those. The plant employs 40 people, and it measures its timber in metres although the invoices are written in centimetres. How many boxes does the factory have now?

Kasper has more deck chairs than his cousin Bea does. He started the season with 224 chairs, and a hotel sold him 39 more. Bea lent him 6 chairs. Storms then wrecked 202 chairs over the winter. The council matched what he had left, leaving him 2 chairs for every chair he owned. Hire is charged in hours although the tickets are printed in minutes. How many deck chairs does Kasper have now?

A hotel had 49 umbrellas in its stand. Guests took 43 umbrellas away over the summer, and 1 was broken in a gale. A lost-property sale then added 79 umbrellas, and a coach party took 59 of them. Half of the stand is empty now, and the hotel has 120 rooms. How many umbrellas are in the stand?

A shoe factory received 167 hides, and each hide was cut into 5 panels. Every panel was then cut into 7 pieces, and each piece was stitched with 4 eyelets. A supplier sent 29 spare eyelets. The factory has 90 sewing stations. How many eyelets are there in total?

On Monday morning a chocolate factory took in 226 sacks of cocoa, and each sack filled 9 vats. By noon every vat had been poured into 8 moulds. In the early afternoon each mould was cut into 6 bars, and a returned order added 80 bars. In the evening every bar was broken into 8 squares. Overnight a taster's box added 5 squares to the count. How many squares does the factory have?
